standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that a constructible subset of a Noetherian space is a finite union of locally closed subsets
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3164-3170 and 3187-3192)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns constructibility into a finite union of locally closed pieces.

standard_prerequisites.name: The decomposition of a Noetherian space into finitely many irreducible components
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 3176-3178)
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the minimal counterexample into components.

core_obligations: (1) implies (2): for an irreducible closed subset the trace is a finite union of locally closed pieces, so if none of them is open in that subset the trace is not dense (proof lines 3163-3170)

(2) implies (1): if the set of closed subsets whose trace is not constructible were nonempty it would have a smallest element; decomposing it into irreducible components either gives a contradiction (more than one component) or reduces to the irreducible case, where the hypothesis gives either an open piece or a strictly smaller closed subset carrying the same trace, contradicting minimality in both cases (proof lines 3171-3199)
proof_roadmap: (1)⇒(2)：E ∩ Z 是有限个局部闭片之并；若没有一片在 Z 中开，则不在 Z 中稠密。
(2)⇒(1)：设反例族非空，取极小元 Y；先按其不可约分支分解——若分支数 >1 则各部分可构造 ⇒ Y 上可构造，矛盾 ⇒ Y 不可约；此时由 (2)，E ∩ Y 或含 Y 的开集（由极小性得 Y ∖ V 上可构造 ⇒ 矛盾），或不在 Y 中稠密（则 E ∩ Y = E ∩ Y' 对某个真闭子集 Y'，由极小性同样得可构造 ⇒ 矛盾）。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement characterizes constructible subsets of a Noetherian space through density conditions on their traces in irreducible closed subsets (author lemma at source lines 3124-3161, label lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian). The proof (source lines 3163-3200) proves one direction from the finite-union description and the converse by a minimal-counterexample argument that first reduces to an irreducible closed subset and then excludes both alternatives of the hypothesis (proof lines 3163-3199). The minimal-counterexample argument is the substance. H3.
